minutes.headline: Committee ratified the revised hybrid learning agreement with the teachers' union and named bargaining team members.
minutes.summary: After an executive session on union negotiations, the committee ratified the revised hybrid agreement that adds live streaming, then assigned members to the teacher, custodial/paraprofessional and cafeteria negotiating teams. what_happened.line: The School Committee ratified the revised hybrid learning agreement with the teachers' union, which adds live streaming; all five members voted yes by roll call.
The committee named Ms. Shapiro and Mrs. Archambault to the teachers' union team, Ms. Kelly to custodial and paraprofessional talks, and Mr. Leighton to cafeteria talks.
The business manager said the custodial union gave notice it wants to bargain its next contract, and last year's teacher agreement ran one year, so a new negotiation is needed.
The extended day program will not open for February vacation week; the April week is to be reevaluated in March.
The committee waived second reading of four policies by roll call and deferred approval of prior minutes to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Contracts with the teachers', custodial, paraprofessional and cafeteria unions set a large share of school payroll costs, so these negotiations shape future school budgets and the town budget, mostly taxes.
Families who rely on extended day care will not have it over February vacation week, and the April week is still undecided.
watch_next: Capital planning wants to raise the base amount that counts as a capital project, with smaller projects absorbed into operating budgets; the minutes give no date for a vote.
The extended day program for the April vacation week is to be reevaluated in March.
